parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing criminalisation of trans identity, border exclusion, or pre-2025 facility exclusion is documented. Pride proceeds openly, courts struck down propaganda bans, and hate-crime and equality law name gender identity. Against this, the record documents a de facto birth-sex men's-system placement of a trans detainee with prolonged isolation, refused protection-ward placement, and forced strip searches, corroborated in 2024 and 2025 and denied by the administration. Public acceptance is very low (79% would not accept LGBT+ neighbours), hate speech has no meaningful official response, police have stood by or refused to investigate attacks, and a service denial over document mismatch was confirmed only after the fact. The custody exposure is the heaviest documented harm; the rest is elevated societal hostility with weak recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border refusal, entry screening or detention of trans visitors. Foreign passports are not shown to be contested.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch is documented only in a bank-service denial, not at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A trans man was held by birth sex in the men's system for about four years, with prolonged solitary-style isolation, forced strip searches and refused protection-ward placement. Reported again in 2025 for three years in isolation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Administration says placement was at his written request; no operative remedy documented. Staff training and stricter penalties are announced but not shown in force.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained on a document or presentation issue could face the same birth-sex placement and isolation regime, since it is institutional practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National penitentiary administration places trans detainees by birth sex in practice and denies protection-unit access. Occupied-region legislation on promotion of non-traditional relations is unsourced in enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Equality Council and courts act on some discrimination, but not on custody.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facility practice governs any detained visitor; the occupied-region law is uncertain and not applied to any individual in the record.

care_services.exposure: Ministry of Health states medical services are accessible regardless of orientation. No documented denial of care to trans visitors. Bank-service denial over appearance mismatch shows services can refuse.
care_services.protection: Equality Council confirmed the bank-service discrimination and recommended preventive measures; implementation unresolved.
care_services.interaction: Document-appearance mismatch can trigger service refusal outside health care; care access itself is not documented as blocked.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Political hate speech rose in election periods; official remarks are described as derogatory. Police stood by in 2008 and 2017 attacks, and refused to investigate a 2019 arson on an LGBT lawyer's car.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Police protected the 2018 Pride march. Propaganda bans of 2012 and 2013 were invalidated by courts.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility framing is present in speech but not in a documented statute against visitors; court rulings partly check it.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for minors or travelling families. Minors' treatment in custody or schools is not in the dossier.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian could face the same document-mismatch and custody exposures as an adult; no minor-specific rule is recorded.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Discrimination and violence described as commonplace; 60% would not accept LGBT+ colleagues; 2008 mob attacks with police standing by; 2017 Pride cancelled after Orthodox group attacks. No trans-specific violence rate with denominator.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Pride now proceeds with police protection in 2018 and 2024. Hate-crime provisions with named grounds since 2022.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recent Pride protection suggests improvement, but visitors outside Pride face social hostility with weak recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Impunity for past violations is reported; the prison administration denied the discrimination claims; hate speech has no meaningful national response.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Equality Council findings, a regional court ruling on the 2008 event, and a ministry pledge to train staff and raise penalties. Operative effect not shown.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Oversight findings recur without changing practice, so recourse does not clearly reduce the custody or street exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: This anchor has a universal border register that excludes trans visitors with appeals almost never granted. The dossier shows no border exclusion, so this case is higher. It is similar in carrying weak institutional remedies, but the custody harm here is less universal than a pervasive entry ban.

This anchor has a health-access ban for nonresidents and discretionary enforcement of visitor restrictions. The dossier documents no comparable care ban, so this case is higher. It is similar in the presence of documented institutional hostility with limited remedy.

This anchor has uneven, sporadic harassment and ejection with formal charges uncommon. The dossier shows comparable street hostility and weak investigation, but adds documented custody placement by birth sex with isolation, so this case is lower.

parsed.synthesis: The documented custody practice (birth-sex placement, isolation, refused protection) is the operative exposure a visitor would meet if detained, and the administration's denial and pledged training are not shown to change it. Societal hostility and police failures add a continuing street exposure with weak recourse. Protective elements (open Pride, struck-down propaganda bans, named hate-crime and equality grounds) are real but do not reach the custody or document-mismatch exposures. No criminal statute against trans identity is documented, which keeps the rating out of the high-risk band, but the unremedied custody harm holds it in the elevated band.
